p: A skating session at the Leisure Plaza is short and sweet, which leaves loads of time for the rest of Milton Keynes. The city is famously green, despite its reputation for roundabouts, and the parks are a real treat. Willen Lake is a favourite for a lakeside walk, with water sports and a play area, and Campbell Park, right next to the centre, has big open lawns and lovely views across the city. Head up to the Light Pyramid on a clear day and you'll see why locals rate it so highly.

Before you head on the ice, a quick word on comfort. Rinks are cold, but you'll warm up fast once you get moving, so go for layers rather than a big coat. Gloves are essential, and thin, long socks beat thick fluffy ones inside hire boots. If it's your first time, start by gliding along the barrier and building up slowly.

For families, it's worth sitting down with the kids before you go and explaining the basics: skate the same way as everyone else, don't stop in the middle, and if you fall, tuck your fingers in and get up quickly. A little pep talk at home saves a lot of nerves at the rink.
If you've got a hockey fan in the group, look out for games on the ice while you're in town. Watching the pros up close is the perfect way to round off a weekend in MK.
